summary: Profile of 62-year-old Welsh actor Owen Teale, best known as Ser Alliser Thorne in Game of Thrones, ahead of his turn as Scrooge in a Melbourne production of A Christmas Carol. It traces his path from a suspension at sixth-form college and a job as Barry the Bear to drama school and a long stage and screen career. Teale discusses playing menacing characters, the fan reaction to killing Jon Snow, and his ambivalence about never becoming a Hollywood leading man.
one_line: Welsh actor Owen Teale, Game of Thrones' Ser Alliser Thorne, discusses his dark roles, unlikely career path and upcoming Scrooge in Melbourne.
key_facts: Owen Teale is a 62-year-old Welsh actor best known as master-at-arms Ser Alliser Thorne in Game of Thrones.
Teale will play Ebenezer Scrooge in a Melbourne production of Jack Thorne's award-winning adaptation of Dickens' A Christmas Carol.
As a teenager Teale was suspended from his sixth-form college for organising a riotous Christmas party, having smuggled in booze in his mother's car.
A teacher, Mr Davies, suggested he work at Barry Island Pleasure Park near Cardiff, where he played Barry the Bear and was sacked after riding the big wheel in costume.
Two co-workers from the Guildford School of Acting suggested he audition there; he was accepted and awarded a study grant.
Ser Alliser Thorne stabbed Jon Snow in the final episode of Season 5 of Game of Thrones, which had 10 million viewers; Jon Snow was played by Kit Harington.
Teale says he finds his dark characters through 'a sense of nothingness' and the emptiness he feels when alone, away from people.
In 1989 he starred in the TV adaptation of Catherine Cookson's The Fifteen Streets alongside Sean Bean.
He won a Tony Award in 1997 for Ibsen's A Doll's House but flew home to London instead of courting Hollywood producers because his wife was about to give birth.
Teale chose a four-year stint with the Royal Shakespeare Company after financing for a bare knuckle fighter film fell through, and William Hurt got another lead role he was offered.
He is currently shooting the second season of the Amazon Prime supernatural thriller The Rig as Lars Hutton.
Other menacing roles include Chief Inspector Philip Osborne in Line of Duty and Peter Knox in A Discovery of Witches.
He praises Toni Collette, his Dream Horse co-star (2020 film), saying 'Toni just raised my game.'
Teale is married to actor Sylvestra Le Touzel; they have daughters Eliza, 25, and Gracie, 21, and he has a son, Ion, from his first marriage.
